newsitem.title: UK: UK oil delays, repairs stunt output growth - Woodmac.
newsitem.headline: UK oil delays, repairs stunt output growth - Woodmac.

text.p: Delayed new North Sea oilfield start-ups and unplanned offshore maintenance have stunted an expected rise in British oil production so far this year, consultants Wood Mackenzie said on Tuesday.
U.K. oil production in the first half of the year averaged 2.53 million bpd, 130,000 bpd below Woodmac projections and up only marginally from the 2.50 million pumped in the first half of 1995.

"Total U.K. output for 1996 is now forecast to average some 2.6 million bpd, a four percent drop on our February forecast and only some 20,000 bpd up on 1995's average of 2.58 million bpd," Woodmac said in a mid-year review.
Woodmac said in February it expected new fields would boost U.K. output to 2.71 million bpd on average this year.
But a slower than expected start to supplies from west of Britain's Douglas and Lennox fields and Harding in the North Sea has put a cap on higher volumes.

In addition, first crude from the Atlantic Basin Foinaven is not now expected until early next year. Operator BP launched an investigation after the discovery of hairline crack in a subsea Foinaven production unit.
Douglas and Lennox together have pumped just 18,000 bpd since starting in March, about a quarter of capacity, because of gas reinjection problems.
Eight new fields are due onstream before the end of the year, but most not until the fourth quarter.
"They will not have a significant impact on the total for the year although the combined initial output of these fields could add an average of 75,000 bpd to last quarter production," said Woodmac.
